messages:
maya: FYI I dug into the TP perf regression after the kernel-selection change this morning. seeing ~15-20% throughput drop on our 8-GPU TP baseline for seq_len=1024 workloads. :frowning:

dennis: Ugh. Any obvious hotspot? comm or compute?

maya: The top-level looks like reduce/collective time spiking for a lot of microbatches. Not compute. The profiler shows frequent tiny reduce messages (~3-8KB each) that make NCCL fall into the ring path and behave poorly.

carla: so small msgs hit ring and we lose parallelism? can you paste the perf sample? :eyes:

maya: paste of condensed trace (from perf script):
```
Timeline (per-step):
 - forward: 120ms
 - kv-cache flush: 6ms (many small ops)
 - reduce start: 2ms (many fragments)
 - reduce (ring): 28ms
 - wait for reduce: 40ms
 - backward: 110ms
 - allreduce tail: 35ms
```
Notice the reduce/rendezvous dominates with many sequential fragments.

ben: Are we sure it's kernel-selection change and not batching heuristic? we tweaked small-batch padding last week.

maya: good call. I toggled the kernel-selection flag back and reran 3 runs — throughput returned to previous baseline. So kernel selection interacts with how we fragment messages.

perf-bot: Alert: TP-eightgpu-seq1024 (stable) regression +18% wall time vs baseline after commit 4f2b. See perf dashboard: https://ci/perf/2161

oliver: could KV-cache behavior be creating more small messages? like more frequent cache flushes -> more skinnier reduces?

maya: yes. On the failing runs KV cache emitted more frequent prefix-update ops because of a subtle change in cache-emit batching thresholds. That created ~3x more reduce fragments per step.

carla: so two orthogonal changes combined: kernel-choice now prefers the tree variant for medium msgs, but because message sizes are reduced we end up in ring fallback more often?

maya: Exactly. The kernel selector picks 'pack-tree' for aggregated sizes > X, but fragmentation reduces aggregate size under X, causing runtime to choose the ring path which has worse overlap for our schedule. We saw a 2.1x increase in all-reduce tail latency for those microbatches.

dennis: Any quick repro we can run locally? script or flags?

maya: repro steps I used: clone the perf harness ->
```
./run_tp_bench --gpus=8 --seq=1024 --kbatch=1 \ 
  --kv-emit-threshold=128 --kernel-selector=auto --profile=timeline.json
```
Then toggle `--kernel-selector=legacy` to compare. Also try `--kv-emit-threshold=512` to force larger fragments.

ben: Can we change kernel selector to prefer tree when fragmentation patterns detected? maybe a cheap heuristic: if kv-flush-rate > N then bias toward tree/aggregate kernels.

oliver: But tree reduces have higher sync points on some topologies. We need to be safe: add a runtime check of commshape and per-step fragment histogram before choosing.

maya: Agreed. My experiment patch does a quick sampling of last 50 fragments and if median frag_size < 8KB then force the pack-aggregating kernel. That recovered ~12% throughput w/o breaking other workloads.

carla: Can you drop the patch as a draft PR? we'll run CI perf matrix. Also need regression test: synthetic workload that triggers kv-flush storm.

maya: Will open PR in a bit. Also adding a perf unit test: `tp_kv_fragmentation.py` that asserts no more than X fragments on the critical path for seq=1024.

perf-bot: Note: automated perf run queued for branch maya/tp-kernel-frag-fix.

dennis: Other follow-ups: (1) audit where kv-emit-threshold changed, (2) add telemetry for frag size distribution in prod traces, (3) long-term: revisit kernel selection cost model.

ben: I'll take (1). oliver can you add telemetry?

oliver: On it. Will add a compact histogram tag to traces (buckets: <4KB, 4-16KB, 16-64KB, >64KB).

carla: thanks everyone. sounds like short-term runtime tweak + telemetry + perf test will mitigate. :thumbsup:

maya: PR up: https://git.redwood/pr/3245 — includes timeline samples and the heuristic. Please review.

ben: review queue. if perf CI looks good we'll ship patch to canary tonight. :rocket:
